scope_note: One conditional local CORE failure; no general or production defect is established. Harness failures, environment limits and subjective UX hypotheses are separate.

items.title: Mission bootstrap stalls in recorded blocked-map conditions
reproduction_steps: Serve pinned CORE Git blobs on loopback; fresh context, Chrome/SwiftShader, 1440×1000.
Block external map resources and load world.html?quality=low.
Wait 25 seconds for CORE civReady without a camera gesture; inspect actual mission controls and state.
evidence: CORE src/earth/app.mjs: map load handler starts civilisation
items.user_impact: In those local offline runs, real committed records return 200 but mission readiness stays false. A later wheel gesture recovered it once. Public-assets runs initialized; production impact is unknown.
items.suggested_fix: CORE team: make local-data mission initialization idempotent and independent of tile availability; show truthful loading/failure states. Verify offline, slow-network and normal public-assets paths on a new commit.
items.verification_scope: Only the retained blocked-resource local setup. Map-dependent source control flow supports a diagnosis, not proof of a renderer root cause or universal failure.

items.title: AI-selected Earth zoom was blocked by the catalog panel
reproduction_steps: Use retained Earth-agent capture and the pre-fix action sequence.
Enter Earth, open catalog, obtain Qwen plan zoom_in, then click the visible zoom control without closing the catalog.
items.user_impact: The only requested AI Earth verification failed. The corrected mission selector was never reached, and evaluation was not started.
items.suggested_fix: HQ now closes the actual catalog before zoom and reopens it for mission selection; future journey Earth flow also waits for the startup camera transition. Requires a separately authorized combined AI retest; no rerun was performed here.
items.verification_scope: Trace explicitly reports ea-panel intercepting pointer events. No hidden/forced click or CORE mutation is an acceptable test substitute.

items.title: Duplicate mission cards violated a unique-selector assumption
reproduction_steps: In second pilot session 4 open Problems & missions.
Use the old unique selector for mission.sf.housing-resilience; two visible buttons match.
items.user_impact: One second-pilot attempt failed despite successful Earth initialization.
items.suggested_fix: Keep first-visible exact-ID selection and record match count. Scripted four-action regression passed; corrected AI selector verification remains incomplete because HQ-001 failed earlier.
items.verification_scope: Duplicate cards are observed UI structure, not evidence that CORE mission opening is defective.

items.title: Quote-anchored AI criticism is not a valid usability verdict
reproduction_steps: Read second-pilot urban-planner and student evaluation outputs.
Compare claims with their own evidence quotes and the rendered dossier.
items.user_impact: Investors or product teams could prioritize false defects or mistake model output for human comprehension.
items.suggested_fix: Retain raw outputs as subjective hypotheses requiring human validation. Add explicit task assertions and reviewed semantic rubrics; never report a returned evaluation as accurate human comprehension.
items.verification_scope: One output alleges missing dates while quoting 2016–2025; another labels evidence-bounded refusal a high-severity issue. These do not establish CORE defects.

items.title: Short screenshot deadlines lose action screenshots under rendering load
reproduction_steps: Inspect first screenshot errors in both pilots.
In the latest Earth run inspect actions 2/3 screenshot timeouts at 2500 ms.
items.user_impact: Latest Earth run retained one PNG and a trace, with two failed screenshot captures. Absence must not be mistaken for a clean visual result.
items.suggested_fix: Use remaining-budget-aware capture deadlines and an explicitly logged screenshot-only retry or trace-frame fallback, without repeating browser tasks or rewriting failed evidence.
items.verification_scope: Trace capture survived; this is evidence quality, not a proven CORE functional defect.

items.title: Public map resource resets and missing optional local-state service
reproduction_steps: Run immutable loopback server with named public map assets enabled.
Inspect request/console logs; the static server cannot serve /.core-local/civ/state.json.
items.user_impact: Two connection resets occurred in the public-assets probe; second pilot logged 13 optional-state 404s including reloads. These add noise and can delay captures.
items.suggested_fix: Record real delivery/error events and renderer/browser settings. Classify the known optional endpoint separately; investigate repeatable missing required assets rather than counting every 404 as a CORE bug.
items.verification_scope: No production backend was tested. Successful imagery delivery and these network failures coexist.

items.title: Contribution council sharing versus browser-local privacy may need clearer emphasis
reproduction_steps: Open the actual mission contribution form and read its consent/vault copy.
Compare first-visitor evaluation output with the actual scope and My CORE contribution disclosure.
items.user_impact: Potential confusion about local queue, encrypted vault and actual publication; no recruited user has demonstrated that confusion.
items.suggested_fix: Consider a concise browser-only/no-publication label next to each action and follow-up acknowledgement. Validate wording with real consented humans before claiming improved comprehension.
items.verification_scope: Synthetic browser fixtures are not human participants. Encrypted-vault storage was not tested by mission-queue checks.

items.title: Large planetary aspiration may overshadow the narrow working demonstration
reproduction_steps: Open the real Earth landing screenshot and What works today disclosure.
Navigate to actual dated mission evidence or Progress to compare scope.
items.user_impact: A first-time visitor may overestimate geographic coverage or verified impact; this is a hypothesis, not a measured human error rate.
items.suggested_fix: Consider moving the current San Francisco scope and working-evidence entry nearer the main CTA while retaining truthful long-term aspiration. Test with humans.
items.verification_scope: CORE already discloses one street and no verified impact. The backlog does not claim those disclaimers are absent.
